title: Roast Pork Belly
subtitle: Slow-roasted pork belly with crisp crackling
excerpt: Pork belly scored, salted, and left overnight so the skin dries out completely, then slow-roasted until the fat renders and the pork is impossibly tender, before a blast of high heat turns the skin into crackling. The most forgiving and rewarding of roasts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast pork belly is eaten across many culinary traditions; the British and Chinese versions are the most widely known outside their respective countries. The British version uses fennel seeds, sage, or apple as common aromatics and is served with apple sauce and crackling; the Chinese version (siu yuk) uses five-spice and soy. Both share the same fundamental technique for the crackling: the skin must be dry, scored deeply, and exposed to very high heat either at the start or end of cooking. Leaving the scored, salted pork belly uncovered in the fridge overnight removes surface moisture from the skin, which is the most effective preparation for crackling. The long, low roast renders the fat without drying the meat.

content.text: The overnight drying step is the most important thing you can do for the crackling. Score the skin with a sharp knife every 1 cm, going through the skin but not into the meat. Rub salt into the scores. Leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. The skin should feel papery and dry when you take it out. Do not cover it; moisture is the enemy of crackling.

items.preparation: boneless; skin on and deeply scored at 1 cm intervals; left uncovered in fridge overnight
sliced; to roast under the pork

content.text: Remove the pork from the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Pat the skin completely dry with kitchen paper. Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Place the fennel, onion, garlic, apple, and thyme in the bottom of a roasting tin. Pour in the wine. Set the pork on top, skin-side up. Rub the salt into the scores.

Roast at the high heat for 30 minutes until the skin is beginning to blister. Reduce to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3. Roast for a further 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is very tender and the fat has rendered. Check that the vegetables do not dry out; add a splash of water if needed.

Increase the heat to 240°C / fan 220°C / gas 9 for the final 10 to 15 minutes to finish the crackling. It should blister and puff completely. If any patches remain soft, use kitchen scissors to cut them away and blast under a very hot grill. Rest the pork for 15 minutes before carving.
